UserHook.rationale: user-supplied Python hook; gets a full state.copy() snapshot by design

__ctype_b_loc.rationale: writes its table through state.memory.store (tracked by CallbackMemoryTracker) and returns a pointer in a synced register

calloc.rationale: same channel as malloc (angr-op0dn.14.1.3). Differential parity, including the zeroed block: test_fallback_parity.py::test_parity[calloc]

fprintf.rationale: same outbound posix channel as fwrite. Parity: test_parity[fprintf]

fputc.rationale: same outbound posix channel as fwrite. Parity: test_parity[fputc]

fwrite.rationale: the bounced stream write now reaches Rust's fd buffer through the outbound posix channel (angr-op0dn.14.1.4), so a later posix.dumps(1) sees it. Differential parity: test_fallback_parity.py::test_parity[fwrite]. The known ~2.8ms/call bounce cost (csyy9) remains a perf, not a correctness, issue

getenv.rationale: reads the posix environ, which is fixed at project init; no Rust-side environ to desync

malloc.rationale: the bounced heap bump now round-trips (angr-op0dn.14.1.3): _create_state_for_callback seeds heap_location from Rust's brk and the resume path pushes it back, so a later native alloc cannot overlap. Differential parity: test_fallback_parity.py::test_parity[malloc]

memmove.rationale: memory-only; on rust_manager._MEMORY_WRITING_PROCS so it gets a full copy+diff

my_scanf.rationale: solve.py UserHook (defcon2016quals_baby-re) that injects symbolic stdin

open.rationale: a bounced open's fd is adopted into Rust's fd table (angr-op0dn.14.1.5) and Rust's own fds are seeded into the callback state (angr-op0dn.14.1.6), so the two sides cannot disagree on an fd number. Differential parity: test_fallback_parity.py::test_parity[open]

operator delete(void*).rationale: routes to angr's free proc; angr's free is a no-op on the heap bump, so nothing is lost

operator new(unsigned long).rationale: routes to angr's malloc proc, whose bounced bump round-trips (angr-op0dn.14.1.3); parity is the malloc row's

pthread_mutex_lock.rationale: angr models it as a no-op returning 0; no Rust-side lock state

pthread_mutex_unlock.rationale: angr models it as a no-op returning 0; no Rust-side lock state

pthread_once.rationale: angr models it as a call-once stub; no Rust-side pthread state exists

readline_hook.rationale: solve.py UserHook (cmu_binary_bomb_partial) that injects a symbolic line

std::allocator<char>::allocator().rationale: C++ stdlib symbol: angr's Python proc (or ReturnUnconstrained) is the reference; no native equivalent exists to diverge from

std::allocator<char>::~allocator().rationale: C++ stdlib symbol: angr's Python proc (or ReturnUnconstrained) is the reference; no native equivalent exists to diverge from

std::basic_ostream<char, std::char_trait.rationale: C++ stdlib symbol: angr's Python proc (or ReturnUnconstrained) is the reference; no native equivalent exists to diverge from

std::basic_string<char, std::char_traits.rationale: C++ stdlib symbol: angr's Python proc (or ReturnUnconstrained) is the reference; no native equivalent exists to diverge from

std::string::length() const.rationale: C++ stdlib symbol: angr's Python proc (or ReturnUnconstrained) is the reference; no native equivalent exists to diverge from

strcmp.rationale: reads synced memory, returns a BV in a synced register; no plugin state touched

strncmp.rationale: reads synced memory, returns a BV in a synced register; no plugin state touched

strncpy.rationale: memory-only; on rust_manager._MEMORY_WRITING_PROCS so it gets a full copy+diff

time.rationale: returns a fresh BV in a synced register; angr's Python proc is the reference
